players.product: enterprise PCIe Gen5 SSD controllers for hyperscaler SSDs

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 73,173,633,575 vs KRW 23,679,326,011 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating profit KRW 16,224,323,601 vs an operating loss of KRW 12,564,211,319 a year earlier; H1 2026 revenue KRW 132,712,085,278 and H1 operating profit KRW 23,910,125,663. H1 net loss of KRW 49,913,846,504 reflects a KRW 73,687,369,663 derivative valuation loss on the 7th convertible bond, whose terms were amended on 06-30-2026
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue KRW 73,173,633,575 (Q2 2025: KRW 23,679,326,011); Q2 operating profit KRW 16,224,323,601; H1 revenue KRW 132,712,085,278; H1 operating profit KRW 23,910,125,663

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 revenue mix: enterprise SSD controllers KRW 108,353 million (81.6%, up from 69.4% of 2025 revenue), finished enterprise SSDs KRW 17,680 million (13.3%), other KRW 6,679 million; all H1 revenue is export (incl. indirect export); by customer location H1 revenue was Asia KRW 94,237,301,744, Korea KRW 31,011,218,771, Americas KRW 7,463,564,763
quarterly_data.figure: controllers KRW 108,353 million (81.6%); SSDs KRW 17,680 million (13.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration (customers >10% of revenue, names undisclosed): Customer A KRW 80,779,146,556 (60.87% of H1 revenue, vs 52.71% in H1 2025), Customer B KRW 28,728,086,581 (21.65%), Customer C KRW 3,810,176,033 (2.87%, vs 14.20%). The company states its first customer was global NAND memory maker A, which adopted FADU controllers for hyperscale-datacenter SSDs on the datacenter's recommendation; supply to hyperscale datacenter A began at end-2021
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A 60.87%; Customer B 21.65%; Customer C 2.87%

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at 06-30-2026 of US$191,755 thousand (total orders US$205,625 thousand, US$13,870 thousand delivered): enterprise SSD controller orders from overseas NAND flash memory manufacturers (US$34,010k, US$30,970k, US$19,000k, US$15,390k, US$14,060k, US$10,260k), a US$6,814k controller order from a domestic semiconductor manufacturer, a US$21,077k SSD order from a global aerospace company (term 02-04-2026 to 03-01-2028) and SSD orders from Macnica Galaxy Inc.; current contract liabilities (customer advances) rose to KRW 64,918,772,536 from KRW 13,939,190,284 at end-2025
quarterly_data.figure: backlog US$191,755 thousand; total orders US$205,625 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: SSD supply contracts with Macnica Galaxy Inc.: US$32,871 thousand (term 11-04-2025 to 11-02-2026, advance received) and US$7,303 thousand (term 05-28-2026 to 11-15-2026); payment expected in Q4 2026

PCIe Gen6 datacenter SSD controller (FC6161) tape-out completed and in discussion with multiple customers; the company says Gen6 offers more than 2x the performance of its Gen5 generation and targets mass supply to more overseas datacenter customers and enterprise storage vendors. Gen5 controllers and Gen5 E1.S / E3.S / U.2 SSDs are in mass production for overseas datacenter customers. Gen6 controller spec: 28.5GB/s sequential read, 20.0GB/s sequential write, 6,900 KIOPS random read

New product lines: two eSSD power chips (PMIC and PLP) passed customer qualification and entered mass production; developing a Gen6 power solution and a PMIC5020-class DDR5 DIMM PMIC; a NAND MUX IC for high-capacity SSDs in development since 10-2025; CXL switch IP basic R&D done, with launch timing being adjusted as NVIDIA NVLink-type alternatives emerge

Supply side: controller chips are bought turnkey from a design house and SSDs are built by an SMT contractor (no own fab). NAND flash price per GB used in its SSDs rose to 18.3 cents in H1 2026 from 6.5 cents in 2025 and 5.8 cents in 2024; H1 purchases were controller ICs KRW 36,179 million and NAND flash KRW 25,739 million (suppliers undisclosed)
quarterly_data.figure: NAND 18.3 cents/GB (2025: 6.5); controller IC purchases KRW 36,179 million; NAND purchases KRW 25,739 million
